label: late original-phase input of z/s/f/x/n/c in sequences starting with i/h/b/u/m/j/d
explanation: Fires almost only in the original phase at t>=3 (89% of mass) and on the <DEL> step (11%). It is essentially silent at t<3 and in the copy phase. Two factors combine. (1) Sequence identity: rate is ~5x when the first original token is i, h, b or u, and ~2x for m, j or d. (2) The current input: it is strongest on z (5.3x), then s, f, x, n and c (2.5-3.5x). It is also biased toward first occurrences of the input token (94% of mass). The conjunction (original phase, t>=3, first_tok in {i,h,b,u,m,j,d}, in_tok in {z,s,f,x,n,c}) gives dev P=0.41, R=0.52, mass recall 0.63, and covers 71% of the top activation quartile. The top activations (about 1.0 of max) are z inputs in sequences that begin with i/h/b/u. Misses include <DEL> steps and other inputs (w, e, r, q) in the same kind of sequences, plus some sequences whose later prefix tokens, not the first, are from that letter set. So the gating looks like a graded hidden-state composition effect, not a sharp rule. Adding <DEL> or requiring in_first lowered F1.
